title: France – Systems consultancy services – Marché cadre PRECY - Prestations Cybersécurité
description: Description détaillée des différents lots : Le présent marché a pour objet la fourniture de prestations en cybersécurité au bénéfice des équipes en charge de la sécurité des systèmes d'information de RTE, au sein de la Direction des Systèmes d'Information et des Télécommunications (DSIT). Dans le cadre de sa politique de sécurité des systèmes d’information, RTE met en œuvre une défense en profondeur, adaptée aux enjeux métiers des différents SI, pour que le SI ne soit pas vecteur de failles de sécurité qui, si elles étaient exploitées, pourraient conduire à des risques sur le système électrique de RTE (divulgation d’informations sensibles, compromission des organes de conduite du réseau, …). Dans ce contexte, une attention particulière est portée au choix des partenaires intervenant dans la sécurité des SI de RTE, afin de s'assurer de leur expertise, fiabilité et engagement dans la protection du système d'information. Le marché est prévu pour une durée de huit (8) ans, comprenant trois (3) années fermes et cinq (5) périodes optionnelles de douze (12) mois chacune. Il sera alloti en quatre (4) lots, dont : - Lot A – Expertises et MCO Ce lot porte sur l’exécution des activités récurrentes et d’expertise indispensable à la sécurité du SI. Exemples d’activités : traitements de tickets, appui technique, interventions en régie, prise en charge des opérations. Ce lot inclut également la mobilisation d’expertises techniques pointues ou rares, pour des prestations telles que de la conception, de l'intégration ou du support de Niveau 3 sur des solutions de sécurité spécifiques, du pentest, de la rétro-ingénierie, la réalisation d’analyses CERT, ou encore la mise en œuvre d’expertises PDIS. La flexibilité du marché permettra ainsi de répondre à des besoins très ciblés exprimés ponctuellement par les équipes d’exploitation ou d’ingénierie. - Lot B – Projets d’ingénierie et études Ce lot cible la réalisation de prestations dans le cadre de projets et études menés par la DSIT de RTE ou en accompagnement des équipes externes. Exemples d’activités : conduite de projets liés à la cybersécurité, production de livrables attendus par les projets clients, études techniques, interventions sous forme de forfaits comportant des jalons et des livrables précis. - Lot C – Gouvernance Ce lot concerne l’élaboration, la mise à jour et la formalisation des politiques de sécurité, en lien étroit avec l’équipe du RSSI. Exemples d’activités : rédaction de référentiels, politiques et procédures sécurité, accompagnement à la conformité réglementaire, suivi de la mise en œuvre des politiques. - Lot D – Plateformes d’intermédiation Ce lot vise à répondre aux besoins spécifiques d’expertise en cybersécurité via le recours à des profils indépendants sur des missions ponctuelles ou très spécialisées. Le périmètre de ce lot, strictement limité aux activités de cybersécurité, est volontairement large afin de permettre l’accès à des compétences rares ou pointues, souvent non définies de façon stricte à l’avance. Les principaux Enjeux du marché à respecter sont : - Sécurisation et résilience du système électrique; - Conformité réglementaire; - Flexibilité et agilité dans la couverture des besoins; - Engagement en matière de responsabilité sociétale et environnementale (RSE).

title: Notice of Intent to Sole Source, Blast and Security Modeling and Simulation Tools and Software Development Training
description: The U.S. Army Corps of Engineers (USACE), Engineer Research and Development Center (ERDC), intends to issue an award to Applied Research Associates, Inc. (UEI: LTMGBJ76B9D8/CAGE: 9R446) on sole source basis for Blast and Security Modeling and Simulation Tools and Software Development Training. ERDC-GSL Structural Mechanics Branch (SMB) requires software development, software modification, and training for software development within ARA developed modeling and simulation (M&S) tools. ARA is the sole developer of the Vulnerability Assessment and Protection Option (VAPO) software and is a leading software developer for modeling and simulation (M&S) tools for rapid estimation of blast damage to buildings. ARA is the sole developer of the Ravel code which is a proprietary computational fluid dynamics solver that provides simulations of blast propagation while using minimal computational resources. The Ravel code is proprietary to ARA. The award will be issued in accordance with 6.103-1(b), One responsible source. The NAICS code for this requirement is 541715 (Research and Development in the Physical, Engineering, and Life Sciences (except Nanotechnology and Biotechnology) with a size standard of 1000 employees. This notice is not a request for competitive quotes or proposals. A solicitation will not be issued. However, all responsible sources may submit a capability statement, proposal, or quotation, which shall be considered by the agency. The information submitted must be provided in sufficient detail to demonstrate the vendor�s ability to fulfill this requirement. The contractor must also provide a description of their past performance in fulfilling requirements which are the same or similar to this requirement and references for each. Information received will be considered solely for the purpose of determining whether to conduct a competitive procurement. A determination by the government not to compete this requirement on a full and open competition basis, based upon responses to this notice, is solely within the discretion of the government. Oral communications are not acceptable in response to this notice. Responses to this requirement may be submitted to Janalyn Dement at Janalyn.H.Dement@usace.army.mil. The solicitation number shall be included in the subject line of the email submission. Responses must be received no later than 15 days from the posted date of this notice.

title: FCI Seagoville Hot Water Generator Replacement
description: Attached is a solicitation package prepared by the Federal Bureau of Prisons, FCI Seagoville for the provision of Hot Water Generator Replacement- located at FCC Seagoville, TX. This package contains all necessary information to submit a quote. Quote Submission Requirements and Instructions The information requested must be submitted by contractors and received on or before the solicitation response date and time. If any of the following information is not received, the Contract Specialist may elect to deem quotes non-compliant or request the required information from one or any of the contractors, whichever is most advantageous to the Government, at the discretion of the Contract Specialist. Questions regarding this requirement may be directed in writing to Camille Gonzalez, Contract Specialist, c9gonzalez@bop.gov Evaluation and Award Methodology: Award of a contract will be made to the quoter who submits a quote, conforming to the requirements of the solicitation, determined to be the best value to the Government considering price and past performance. The following factors will be evaluated: Price: Price shall be evaluated utilizing the total aggregate pricing offered by the quoter. Past Performance: The Contractor Performance Assessment Reporting System (CPARS) at www.cpars.gov and/or the professional references submitted with quotes, and/or any other relevant information available to the Contract Specialist may be used for past performance evaluation. SAM Registration: All potential quoters are advised that this solicitation included the provision at FAR 52.204.7, System for Award Management, which requires that an offeror be registered in SAM when submitting an offer or quote and continue to be registered throughout the duration of the task order. Quoters should include their Unique Entity Identifier (UEI) Number in their quotation. Failure to complete the registration procedures outlined in this clause may result in elimination from consideration for award. PTAC: If you have questions about the System for Award Management (SAM), Government procedures in general, or need assistance in the preparation of your quote, a local Procurement Technical Assistance Center (PTAC) may be able to help. The Procurement Technical Assistance Program was authorized by Congress in 1985 in an effort to expand the number of businesses capable of participating in the Government marketplace. To locate a PTAC near you, go to http://www.aptac-us.org. Freedom of Information Act: The Freedom of Information Act (FOIA) and its amendments have resulted in an increasing number of requests to Federal Agencies for copies of quotes from other than Government sources. The quoter should identify information in its quote it believes should be withheld from these sources, on the basis it consists of "trade secrets and commercial or financial information obtained from a person and privileged or confidential" (exemption (b)(4)of the (FOIA). This identification will assist in the decision by a responsible federal official to disclose or withhold the requested information. If a quoter considers elements of its quote to be exempt under FOIA, ensure the following notice is annotated on the titlepage of the quote: "Elements of this document, as identified on individual pages, are considered by the submitter to be privileged or confidential trade secrets or commercial or financial information not subject to mandatory disclosure under the Freedom of Information Act. Material considered privileged or confidential on this basis is contained on pages ____." The quote must annotate each individual item it considers privileged or confidential under the FOIA exemption with the following notice: "The data or information is considered confidential or privileged, and not subject to mandatory disclosure under the FOIA." All information in an offeror's quote not designated may be subject to automatic public disclosure if it is requested under the FOIA. It must be emphasized that under the FOIA, no information is automatically exempt form public disclosure. However, no disclosures will be made without careful evaluation, giving due regard to the need for safeguarding material considered privileged or confidential by the quoter. It is the Department of Justice policy to withhold whenever possible, material that is genuinely privileged or confidential. II. Pre-Quote Questions: Any questions relating to the solicitation after the closing of the pre-quote conference/site visit shall be sent in WORD FORMAT to Camille Gonzalez, Contract Specialist, via email at c9gonzalez@bop.gov no later than ONE WEEK PRIOR TO SOLICITATION CLOSING DATE, at 10:00 am EST. In order to provide sufficient response time prior to the quote due date, the Government is establishing the above cut-off date for questions about the solicitation. All quoters shall quote/ offer in accordance with the current solicitation to include all amendments (if any) as issued by the Contract Specialist only. Funds are not presently available for this solicitation. No award will be made under this solicitation until funds are made available and confirmed in writing by the Contracting Specialist. The Government reserves the right to cancel this solicitation at any time; either before or after the closing date. In the event of cancellation, the Government shall have no obligation to reimburse any quoter for any costs incurred in connection with the preparation or submission of its quote

This contract specifically addresses supply and delivery of multiple steam traps throughout USCGC HEALY (WAGB 20), providing steam for heating the ship, supporting HEALY�s ability to operate for extended periods and perform scientific research in Arctic climates. To establish Technical Capability (Pass/Fail), the quotation must demonstrate a clear understanding of the work statement requirements, conform strictly to all specifications in the attached Statement of Work, and provide any adequate capability and corporate experience documentation required by the solicitation. Failure to meet these criteria will render the quotation unacceptable. The Government will evaluate recent (completed within the last three years) and relevant past performance to assess the likelihood of successful performance. Past performance will be evaluated on an acceptable or unacceptable basis. To receive an acceptable rating, past performance must demonstrate a rating of satisfactory or higher performance of similar work. Offerors without recent or relevant past performance will be assessed as "Neutral" and considered acceptable for award. Past performance demonstrating marginal or below performance is unacceptable. Offerors shall identify all subcontractors anticipated to perform work under this contract. For each subcontractor, the offeror shall provide the subcontractor�s name, address, point of contact, phone number, the specific work items/specifications they will perform, and the percentage of work they will execute. Submissions must be complete, clear, and presented in a format that allows effective evaluation by the Government. Submit all questions via email to the points of contact identified in this notice. The Government will not accept telephone inquiries. Submit offers on a firm-fixed-price basis. Prices must be all-inclusive and must cover all costs associated with providing the services, including but not limited to labor, materials, equipment, supervision, transportation, and any other costs. The Government may consider offers nonresponsive if they include conditional pricing, price escalation language, or statements indicating that prices are subject to adjustment based on future costs or fees. Material considered privileged or confidential on this basis is contained on pages ____." description: Attached is a solicitation package prepared by the Federal Bureau of Prisons, FCI Seagoville for the provision of Building Elevator Renovation - located at FCC Seagoville, TX. Quote Submission Requirements and Instructions The information requested must be submitted by contractors and received on or before the solicitation response date and time. Questions regarding this requirement may be directed in writing to Camille Gonzalez, Contract Specialist, c9gonzalez@bop.gov Evaluation and Award Methodology: Award of a contract will be made to the quoter who submits a quote, conforming to the requirements of the solicitation, determined to be the best value to the Government considering price and past performance. The following factors will be evaluated: Price: Price shall be evaluated utilizing the total aggregate pricing offered by the quoter. Past Performance: The Contractor Performance Assessment Reporting System (CPARS) at www.cpars.gov and/or the professional references submitted with quotes, and/or any other relevant information available to the Contract Specialist may be used for past performance evaluation. SAM Registration: All potential quoters are advised that this solicitation included the provision at FAR 52.204.7, System for Award Management, which requires that an offeror be registered in SAM when submitting an offer or quote and continue to be registered throughout the duration of the task order. Quoters should include their Unique Entity Identifier (UEI) Number in their quotation. Failure to complete the registration procedures outlined in this clause may result in elimination from consideration for award. PTAC: If you have questions about the System for Award Management (SAM), Government procedures in general, or need assistance in the preparation of your quote, a local Procurement Technical Assistance Center (PTAC) may be able to help. The Procurement Technical Assistance Program was authorized by Congress in 1985 in an effort to expand the number of businesses capable of participating in the Government marketplace. To locate a PTAC near you, go to http://www.aptac-us.org. Freedom of Information Act: The Freedom of Information Act (FOIA) and its amendments have resulted in an increasing number of requests to Federal Agencies for copies of quotes from other than Government sources. The quoter should identify information in its quote it believes should be withheld from these sources, on the basis it consists of "trade secrets and commercial or financial information obtained from a person and privileged or confidential" (exemption (b)(4)of the (FOIA). This identification will assist in the decision by a responsible federal official to disclose or withhold the requested information. If a quoter considers elements of its quote to be exempt under FOIA, ensure the following notice is annotated on the titlepage of the quote: "Elements of this document, as identified on individual pages, are considered by the submitter to be privileged or confidential trade secrets or commercial or financial information not subject to mandatory disclosure under the Freedom of Information Act. Material considered privileged or confidential on this basis is contained on pages ____." The quote must annotate each individual item it considers privileged or confidential under the FOIA exemption with the following notice: "The data or information is considered confidential or privileged, and not subject to mandatory disclosure under the FOIA." All information in an offeror's quote not designated may be subject to automatic public disclosure if it is requested under the FOIA. It must be emphasized that under the FOIA, no information is automatically exempt form public disclosure. However, no disclosures will be made without careful evaluation, giving due regard to the need for safeguarding material considered privileged or confidential by the quoter. It is the Department of Justice policy to withhold whenever possible, material that is genuinely privileged or confidential. II. Pre-Quote Questions: Any questions relating to the solicitation after the closing of the pre-quote conference/site visit shall be sent in WORD FORMAT to Camille Gonzalez, Contract Specialist, via email at c9gonzalez@bop.gov no later than ONE WEEK PRIOR TO SOLICITATION CLOSING DATE, at 10:00 am CST. description: 9/10/2026 - Update to solicitation Solicitation deadline has been extended to 16 September 2026 at 12:00PM EDT. ___________________________________________________________________ 9/9/2026 - Update on Solicitation Please reference Attachment 5 for Q&A document. ___________________________________________________________________ Combined Synopsis/Solicitation AFLCMC/PZI Installation Contracting Support Wright Patterson AFB, OH 45323 Date: 31 August 2026 Title: AFIT River Rock Border Request for Quote (RFQ) / Solicitation Number: FA860126Q0113 Quotes Due: 14 September 2026 at 12:00 PM EST Contact Point(s): Chris Hall, Contract Specialist; christopher.hall.113@us.af.mil Contact Point(s): Linh Jameson, Contracting Officer; linh.jameson@us.af.mil Description: This is a combined synopsis/solicitation for commercial products or commercial services prepared in accordance with RFO Part 12. This announcement constitutes the only solicitation. Offers are being requested and a separate written solicitation will not be issued. Solicitation number FA860126Q0113 is issued as a request for quotation (RFQ) for a river rock border landscaping requirement at the Air Force Institute of Technology (AFIT) located at Wright Patterson Air Force Base. This acquisition is set-aside for small business concerns under NAICS code 561730 � Landscaping Services with a small business size of $9,500,000. This solicitation incorporates provisions and clauses by reference. The full text of provisions and clauses may be accessed electronically at www.acquisition.gov. Receives a rating of �Acceptable� on the Technical Capability evaluation factor. Contains the lowest evaluated price (TEP), provided that the TEP is not unbalanced and is fair and reasonable. The Government also reserves the right to cancel this solicitation, either before or after the closing date. 1. Requirement: This requirement is for river rock border landscaping work in accordance with the Performance Work Statement (PWS) dated 28 Aug 2026. 2. Period of Performance: To be completed no later than 120 days after receipt of order (ARO) to Wright Patterson AFB, Ohio. This is inclusive of lead time and installation. 3. Provisions and Clauses: See solicitation attachment for applicable provisions and clauses that apply to this acquisition. NOTE 2: In accordance with R-DFARS 252.204-7021 and R-DFARS 252.204-7025, a CMMC Level 1 assessment is the mandatory minimum requirement for all offerors bidding with the Department of War. Under CMMC Level 1, all offerors must demonstrate full compliance by self-certifying with the 15 basic safeguarding requirements for Federal Contract Information (FCI) outlined in RFO 52.240-93(b)(1). Once your organization has confirmed its compliance with these 15 requirements, you must enter this self-certification into the Supplier Performance Risk System (SPRS) module within PIEE (https://piee.eb.mil). Contract award cannot be made to any offeror that is not fully compliant and whose assessment results are not properly recorded in the system of record. You must verify the CMMC Level required for this award by checking the provisions and clauses within the solicitation. 4. Quotes Due Date: Quotes must be submitted electronically to the Contract Specialist via e-mail at christopher.hall.113@us.af.mil and Contracting Officer at linh.jameson@us.af.mil. It is the responsibility of the offeror to ensure that the quote and its attachments are received. Any correspondence sent via e-mail must contain the subject line �FA860126Q0113, AFIT River Rock Border� The entire quotation must be contained in a single e-mail that does not exceed 5 megabytes including attachments, if any. E-mails with compressed files are not permitted. Therefore, if the specified subject line is not included, the e-mail may not get through the e-mail filters. Also be advised that .zip or .exe files are not allowable attachments and may be deleted by the email filters at Wright-Patterson. If sending attachments with email, ensure only .pdf, .doc, .docx, .xls or .xlsx documents are sent. The email filter may delete any other form of attachments. All quotes shall be in whole dollars and conform to the Contract Line-Item Number (CLIN) structure of attached solicitation. 5. title: Operations Research Systems Analysis (ORSA) Support Services for Capability Program Executive Enterprise Software and Services (CPE ES2)
description: U.S. Army Contracting Command � Rock Island (ACC-RI), on behalf of the Capability Program Executive Enterprise Software & Services (CPE ES2), Fort Belvoir, VA, intends to award a new non-competitive, single-award Firm-Fixed-Price Labor Hours (FFP-LH) contract to Augur Consulting, Inc. (CAGE Code: 659X0, UEID: ZLJNJG6DRZJ5), located at 1400 Crystal Dr. Suite 800, Arlington, VA 22202. The proposed contract will be awarded on a sole-source basis under the authority of Revolutionary Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) Overhaul 6.103-1, "Only One Responsible Source and No Other Supplies or Services Will Satisfy Agency Requirements". This procurement is to provide highly specialized Operations Research and Systems Analysis (ORSA), cost estimating, and financial management support services. The scope of services covers the full range of ORSA methodologies, including parametric cost modeling (utilizing ACEIT, COCOMO, and SEER-SEM), life-cycle cost estimating, schedule risk analysis, data science, and advanced analytics. These services are critical to support informed acquisition, programming, and resource prioritization decisions across the CPE ES2 portfolio. THIS NOTICE OF INTENT IS NOT A REQUEST FOR COMPETITIVE PROPOSALS/QUOTES. However, all responsible sources who believe they can meet the full scope of this requirement may submit a capability statement, which shall be considered by the agency. Information received will be evaluated solely for the purpose of market research. A determination by the Government not to compete this requirement based upon responses received as a result of this notice is solely within the discretion of the Government.

title: GL Mobile App
description: The Centers for Disease Control and Prevention intends to award a sole source firm fixed price purchase order to Mobomo LLC for continued maintenance of the CDC Sexually Transmitted Infections (STI) Treatment Guidelines Mobile Applications (STI Tx Guide app, iOS and Android) and the associated web-based administrative backend panel, in accordance with the Performance Work Statement. Mobomo LLC is uniquely qualified to perform this work. Mobomo LLC was awarded the prior contract (75D30121F12792) in 2021 to complete testing and development of the STI Tx Guide apps and the web-based administrative backend panel, and has since maintained these systems, including their underlying source code, technical architecture, Ruby on Rails backend environment, CDC Bitbucket repository structure, and integration with CDC's cloud and Section 508 compliance requirements. As a result, Mobomo LLC possesses institutional knowledge of the existing codebase, documented and undocumented technical dependencies, and established working relationships with CDC's Office of Informatics project team that would not be readily available to a new contractor. The DSTDP STI Treatment Guidelines are undergoing an extensive update, and continued, uninterrupted access to the mobile application is required for healthcare providers in the field during this period. Transitioning maintenance responsibilities to a new contractor at this time would introduce unacceptable risk of service disruption, given the need for in-depth familiarity with the existing apps' functionality, the backend panel, ongoing bug resolution processes, and compliance obligations (including Section 508 and the SHARE IT Act). A new contractor would require a substantial onboarding and knowledge-transfer period, during which the risk of gaps in app functionality, delayed bug fixes, or lapses in the 24-hour email response requirement to etools@cdc.gov would materially increase. This contract action is for information technology maintenance and support services for which the Government intends to solicit and negotiate with only one source under the authority of FAR 13.106-1(b) (Simplified Acquisition Procedures). This notice of intent is not a request for competitive quotations; however, all quotations/responses received within three (3) calendar days (September 16, 2026) of the issuance of this notice shall be considered by the Government. A determination by the Government not to compete this proposed contract based upon responses to this notice is solely within the discretion of the Government. Information received will normally be considered solely for the purpose of determining whether to conduct a competitive procurement. Any response should be emailed to the Contracting Officer, Jasmine Powell at jpowell5@cdc.gov by September 16, 2026 at 12:00 p.m. EST.

title: Semi-Automatic Rifles for Feral Swine Program
description: This requirement supports the United States Department of Agriculture (USDA), Animal and Plant Health Inspection Service (APHIS), Wildlife Services (WS), National Feral Swine Program (NFSP). Wildlife Services serves as the Nation�s wildlife damage management authority, and the NFSP is to protect agricultural and natural resources, property, animal health, and human health and safety by managing damage caused by feral swine in the United States and its Territories. NFSP has worked to reduce and eradicate feral swine, along with monitoring feral swine for pathogens that affect domestic swine, other livestock, and human health, impacting trade and commerce since 2014. Feral swine occur throughout most of the United States and many US territories. To support the NFSP damage management and potential emergency response activities due to a newly introduce foreign animal disease (FAD), USDA seeks to procure long rifles of differing calibers to help reduce feral swine populations and use as depopulation methos for large scale emergency response FAD events. The contractor shall provide nine (9) .223/5.56 NATO semi-automatic long rifles and nine (9) .308 semi-automatic long rifles. All rifles must meet or exceed the requirements listed in Section 4.0. The contractor shall include delivery, warranty, and all applicable operator documentation. This is a combined synopsis/solicitation for commercial items prepared in accordance with the format in FAR Part 12. This announcement constitutes the only solicitation. Quotations are being requested and a separate written solicitation will not be issued. Solicitation number 12639526Q0300 is issued as a Request for Quotation (RFQ) for Semi-Automatic Rifles. This acquisition is set-aside for small business concerns. The applicable North American Industry Classification Standard Code is 332994 Small Arms, Ordnance, and Ordnance Accessories Manufacturing The small business size standard is 1,000 Employees This acquisition is a Total Small Business Set-Aside. All responsible sources may submit a quotation which will be considered by the agency.

title: USACE SPK DBB Construction - Natomas Reach I Contract 2 - Sacramento, CA
description: The United States Army Corps of Engineers (USACE) Sacramento District (SPK) requires design-bid-build (DBB) construction services to be performed in support of the Natomas Reach I Contract 2 (RIC2) at Sacramento, California (CA). The project supports the American River Common Features (ARCF), Natomas Basin Project, located within the great Sacramento region of California. RIC2 is a continuation of Contract 1 which provided cutoff walls for seepage mitigation in the levees for the entire reach of Natomas Reach I, extending from Northgate Boulevard to Gateway Oaks Drive along the American River levee. Contract 2 project requires flattening the landside slope along the American River from Gateway Oaks Drive to the Northgate Boulevard and along the NEMDC. Total length of slope flattening is approximately 2.18 miles and includes site excavation and re-use of approximately 15,000 cubic yard levee embankment fill and borrow site excavation and import of approximately 12,000 cubic yard levee embankment fill. The work also includes the relocation of utilities, construction of a 12-foot maintenance road at the landside toe, and tree removal. Activities that impact the levee prism will only be permitted between 15 April and 1 November. The estimated cost for the project is $10,000,000 to $13,000,000. The Government intends to solicit an Invitation for Bids (IFB) that will result in award of a firm-fixed price contract. The North American Industrial Classification System (NAICS) code is 237990, Other Heavy and Civil Engineering Construction. The small business size standard for this NAICS, as established by the United States Small Business Administration (SBA), is $45,500,000.00 annual revenue The Product and Service Code (PSC) is Y1LC, Construction of Tunnels and Subsurface Structures. The solicitation is issued as a total small business set-aside through the Procurement Integrated Enterprise Environment (PIEE - https://piee.eb.mil) and Governmentwide Point of Entry, the System for Award Management (SAM - www.SAM.gov).The Government will conduct a pre-bid conference and site walk on 17 August 2026. The solicitation and attachments are posted in Portable Document Format (.pdf) which will require Adobe Acrobat Reader to open and view files. Adobe Acrobat Reader may be downloaded free of charge at http://www.adobe.com/products/reader. All prospective Offerors should be registered in the PIEE system at least one (1) week prior to the anticipated bid due date. Registration is not required to download any forthcoming solicitation documents, plans, and/or specifications, but IS required to submit a bid. Copies of the solicitation and attachments are available for inspection when accessed through PIEE. Failure to register in PIEE will prevent submission of bids as the Government will not accept them by any other means. See linked PIEE registration instructions and web-based training for information about how to access the PIEE Solicitation Module and submit bids. All prospective Offerors must be registered in SAM before the anticipated solicitation closing date. Please see the SAM website for information about SAM registration requirements and approval timelines. USACE will not notify prospective Offerors of any changes to the solicitation; Offerors must monitor PIEE and SAM for the solicitation to be posted, and for any posted changes or amendments. The ONLY Interested Vendors / Plan Holders / Bidders List is available through SAM.gov; Contractors are responsible for identifying their entity as an interested vendor and contacting other interested vendors. USACE SPK will not review capabilities statements submitted in response to this posting or coordinate partnering arrangements between parties. description: Combined Synopsis/Solicitation NOTICE: Solicitation number HT940626QB004 is issued as a request for quote (RFQ). Solicitation number HT940626QB004 is issued as a request for quote for PrograMill 7 Dental Mill System and Maintenance Services. Product/Service Code: 6520 - Dental Instruments, Equipment, and Supplies Competition Approach: Other than Full and Open Competition, RFO FAR 6.103-1, Only One Responsible Source and No Other Supplies or Services Will Satisfy Agency Requirements. Description of Requirement: The Defense Health Agency (DHA) intends to procure a firm-fixed-price (FFP) contract for non-personal services to provide a PrograMill Dental Mill System, along with associated annual maintenance and repair services in support of U.S. Dental Laboratory located at Eisenhower Army Medical Center, Fort Gordon, Georgia. title: Coburn Gore LPOE Art in Architecture Project
description: Document Added: 0332CG-AIA- Questions & Answers Dated 04 August 2026 The U.S. General Services Administration (GSA) Art in Architecture Program commissions American artists (citizens and Lawful Permanent Residents or Permanent Workers of the United States) to create publicly scaled and permanently installed artworks for Federal buildings nationwide. GSA announces an opportunity for a Federal art commission in conjunction with the new construction of the Coburn Gore Land Port of Entry (LPOE) in Coburn, Maine. The new facility will strengthen supply chains, improve operational capabilities and facility infrastructure, spur economic growth, and bolster the country�s security. The project will provide a fully operational LPOE that coordinates with the tra?c ?ow and operations of the Canadian port of entry at Saint-Augustin-de-Woburn Quebec, Port of Entry. The project will provide a new port that allows Customs and Border Protection to more efficiently carry out its agency mission, their operations and interactions with the public. GSA allocates one-half of one percent (0.5%) of the estimated construction costs of new or modernized Federal facilities for art commissions. The art budget for this project is estimated to be between $275,000 to $400,000. One or more artists will be awarded a fixed-price contract for a commission. Artists who wish to be considered for this GSA art commission must submit application materials to GSA by the SAM Contract Opportunity�s Response Date. Artists may also elect to be considered for all future GSA art commissions by submitting application materials to GSA�s National Artist Registry (Registry). Instructions on how to submit application materials and join the Registry are available on the following Web site: https://www.gsa.gov/real-estate/design-and-construction/art-in-architecturefine-arts/art-in-architecture-program/art-in-architecture-national-artist-registry All artists who wish to be considered as candidates for a commission at the LPOE in Coburn Gore, ME must have their application materials submitted and received by GSA by 12:00 PM Eastern Time on 16 September 2026. Artists� submissions received after the deadline will not be considered for this project but will be eligible for consideration on future GSA commissions alongside the other artists on the Registry. Artists already on the Registry need not resubmit but may elect to update their information prior to the deadline. GSA evaluates artists based on the following criteria: the media, materials, content and style of the artist�s past work, along with the artist�s past performance and experience with commissions or projects similar to the one described in this synopsis. Shortlisted artists will be contacted and asked to submit additional information, including a statement that the artist can perform the work associated with the GSA commission within the identified budget. GSA will count the combined weight of all the selection criteria as significantly more important than price. At minimum, the scope of services for this commission will require collaboration with the lead designer selected for the land port of entry project; travel to the project site; development and presentation of preliminary and final concepts; fabrication of the artwork; participation in meetings and conservation reviews as necessary; delivery and installation of the artwork; professional documentation of, and detailed maintenance planning for the artwork at the project site. For informational purposes: Artists selected for the contract award must be Permanent Residents or Citizens of the United States of America. Artists selected for the contract award will be required to have an active registration in the System for Award Management (SAM) at the time of award. Instructions for creating an account and activating registration in SAM may be found at www.sam.gov. Artists selected for the contract award will be required to renew the registration in SAM on an annual basis for the duration of the project. In accordance with Executive Order (EO) 13934, agencies should prioritize the commission of works of art that portray historically significant Americans or events of American historical significance or illustrate the ideals upon which our Nation was founded. Inquiries concerning the project should be directed to the following email address: Molly.Lewis@gsa.gov and reference the synopsis number in the subject line.

title: GL Mobile App
description: The Centers for Disease Control and Prevention intends to award a sole source firm fixed price purchase order to Mobomo LLC for continued maintenance of the CDC Sexually Transmitted Infections (STI) Treatment Guidelines Mobile Applications (STI Tx Guide app, iOS and Android) and the associated web-based administrative backend panel, in accordance with the Performance Work Statement. Mobomo LLC is uniquely qualified to perform this work. Mobomo LLC was awarded the prior contract (75D30121F12792) in 2021 to complete testing and development of the STI Tx Guide apps and the web-based administrative backend panel, and has since maintained these systems, including their underlying source code, technical architecture, Ruby on Rails backend environment, CDC Bitbucket repository structure, and integration with CDC's cloud and Section 508 compliance requirements. As a result, Mobomo LLC possesses institutional knowledge of the existing codebase, documented and undocumented technical dependencies, and established working relationships with CDC's Office of Informatics project team that would not be readily available to a new contractor. The DSTDP STI Treatment Guidelines are undergoing an extensive update, and continued, uninterrupted access to the mobile application is required for healthcare providers in the field during this period. Transitioning maintenance responsibilities to a new contractor at this time would introduce unacceptable risk of service disruption, given the need for in-depth familiarity with the existing apps' functionality, the backend panel, ongoing bug resolution processes, and compliance obligations (including Section 508 and the SHARE IT Act). A new contractor would require a substantial onboarding and knowledge-transfer period, during which the risk of gaps in app functionality, delayed bug fixes, or lapses in the 24-hour email response requirement to etools@cdc.gov would materially increase. This contract action is for information technology maintenance and support services for which the Government intends to solicit and negotiate with only one source under the authority of FAR 13.106-1(b) (Simplified Acquisition Procedures). This notice of intent is not a request for competitive quotations; however, all quotations/responses received within three (3) calendar days (September 16, 2026) of the issuance of this notice shall be considered by the Government. A determination by the Government not to compete this proposed contract based upon responses to this notice is solely within the discretion of the Government. Information received will normally be considered solely for the purpose of determining whether to conduct a competitive procurement. Any response should be emailed to the Contracting Officer, Jasmine Powell at jpowell5@cdc.gov by September 16, 2026 at 12:00 p.m. EST.

title: USACE SPK DBB Construction - Natomas Reach I Contract 2 - Sacramento, CA
description: The United States Army Corps of Engineers (USACE) Sacramento District (SPK) requires design-bid-build (DBB) construction services to be performed in support of the Natomas Reach I Contract 2 (RIC2) at Sacramento, California (CA). The project supports the American River Common Features (ARCF), Natomas Basin Project, located within the great Sacramento region of California. RIC2 is a continuation of Contract 1 which provided cutoff walls for seepage mitigation in the levees for the entire reach of Natomas Reach I, extending from Northgate Boulevard to Gateway Oaks Drive along the American River levee. Contract 2 project requires flattening the landside slope along the American River from Gateway Oaks Drive to the Northgate Boulevard and along the NEMDC. Total length of slope flattening is approximately 2.18 miles and includes site excavation and re-use of approximately 15,000 cubic yard levee embankment fill and borrow site excavation and import of approximately 12,000 cubic yard levee embankment fill. The work also includes the relocation of utilities, construction of a 12-foot maintenance road at the landside toe, and tree removal. Activities that impact the levee prism will only be permitted between 15 April and 1 November. The estimated cost for the project is $10,000,000 to $13,000,000. The Government intends to solicit an Invitation for Bids (IFB) that will result in award of a firm-fixed price contract. The North American Industrial Classification System (NAICS) code is 237990, Other Heavy and Civil Engineering Construction. The small business size standard for this NAICS, as established by the United States Small Business Administration (SBA), is $45,500,000.00 annual revenue The Product and Service Code (PSC) is Y1LC, Construction of Tunnels and Subsurface Structures. The solicitation is issued as a total small business set-aside through the Procurement Integrated Enterprise Environment (PIEE - https://piee.eb.mil) and Governmentwide Point of Entry, the System for Award Management (SAM - www.SAM.gov).The Government will conduct a pre-bid conference and site walk on 17 August 2026. The solicitation and attachments are posted in Portable Document Format (.pdf) which will require Adobe Acrobat Reader to open and view files. Adobe Acrobat Reader may be downloaded free of charge at http://www.adobe.com/products/reader. All prospective Offerors should be registered in the PIEE system at least one (1) week prior to the anticipated bid due date. Registration is not required to download any forthcoming solicitation documents, plans, and/or specifications, but IS required to submit a bid. Copies of the solicitation and attachments are available for inspection when accessed through PIEE. Failure to register in PIEE will prevent submission of bids as the Government will not accept them by any other means. See linked PIEE registration instructions and web-based training for information about how to access the PIEE Solicitation Module and submit bids. All prospective Offerors must be registered in SAM before the anticipated solicitation closing date. Please see the SAM website for information about SAM registration requirements and approval timelines. USACE will not notify prospective Offerors of any changes to the solicitation; Offerors must monitor PIEE and SAM for the solicitation to be posted, and for any posted changes or amendments. The ONLY Interested Vendors / Plan Holders / Bidders List is available through SAM.gov; Contractors are responsible for identifying their entity as an interested vendor and contacting other interested vendors. USACE SPK will not review capabilities statements submitted in response to this posting or coordinate partnering arrangements between parties. Contractors should check SAM.gov frequently for changes to the interested vendors list and this Notice. ------------ Amendment 0001 is issued to: 1. Extend the bid due date to 16 September 2026, 0900 / 09:00 AM Pacific Time. 2. Extend the bid opening to 16 September 2026, 1200 / 12:00 PM Pacific Time. 3. Revise solicitation attachments A05, A06, and A07. 4. Add new solicitation attachments: A06, A09, A10, A11, A12, A13, A14, and A15. 5. Revise solicitation section 00 10 00, CLIN Schedule. Update section 00 21 00 to require submission of A15, Bid Schedule, in lieu of the SF 1442 section 00 10 00, CLIN Schedule. PLEASE NOTE - New and revised attachments are posted on www.SAM.gov only, due to current PIEE system errors.

title: Galveston HVAC Repair/Replacement
description: The purpose of this amendment 0001 is to clarify CAR 1352.246-70, as well as provide an updated revised SOW and respond to the questions received for Solicitation No. 1333MF26Q0110. Combined Synopsis Solicitation: 1333MF26Q0110 CAR 1352.246-70 final inspection and acceptance will occur at the NOAA Galveston facility An updated Revised Statement of Work is included in this amendment 0001 as an attachment to the amended solicitation. Revisions are clearly identified in �red font�. Response to Questions: Q&A #1 Solicitation_1333MF26Q0110_FD-26-517 (Galveston HVAC repairs/Replacements) All questions were due from vendors by 10am EST 9/10 Q1-Please confirm the required nominal capacity for the three Mitsubishi PKA-A30KA6 replacements. The SOW describes these as 2-ton systems, while the model designation appears to indicate a different nominal capacity. A1 - There are two (2) 2 � ton and one (1) 2 ton machines in the Turtle Hospital. Clarified in more detail for question 14. Q2-Please provide the required capacity of each indoor head serving the new 3-ton dual-head system in the Turtle Barn Aquaculture Area. A2- should be a (2) two ton unit with each head being a one (1) ton unit Q3-Please confirm the voltage, phase, available breaker capacity, and whether the existing electrical circuits may be reused. A3 - Existing circuits will be reused. The new breaker for the turtle barn will be added by NOAA, it will be a 208volt Q4-Please clarify whether the base-year CLIN must include all four quarterly preventive-maintenance visits in addition to the five-system installation. A4 - Yes, base year must include quarterly preventive maintenance. Q5-Please confirm the correct option-year CLIN numbering. The solicitation identifies the option CLINs as 0002�0005 in one section and 1001�4001 in another. A5) Option CLINS will either be 0002-0005 or 1001-4001, no final decision has been made Q6-Please identify the acceptable coastal-corrosion coating standards, approved products, and required manufacturer or warranty documentation. A6 - Both the interior and exterior units must have appropriate coastal coating to meet the Galveston Climate and proximity to the ocean/sea air. Q7-Please confirm that final inspection and acceptance will occur at the NOAA Galveston facility. CAR 1352.246-70 currently identifies the NMFS Miami campus as the place of acceptance. A7) Final inspection will occur at the Galveston Facility Q8-Please provide any site-visit measurements, photographs, attendance notes, or other information available to prospective offerors who could not attend the scheduled walkthrough. A8) All Q&A from the site visit is located within this Q&A document and Amendment to the solicitation Q9-Please clarify whether NOAA will issue tax-exempt purchasing documentation for materials incorporated into the project. A9) The Federal government does not pay taxes, however we can not dictate state and local tax requirements on vendors. NOAA will not be issuing tax exempt purchasing documentation for material purchasing, however the contract itself will be tax exempt as the Federal Government does not pay taxes. Q10-Please confirm whether monthly-equivalent pricing is required only for preventive-maintenance services or also for the one-time installation under the base CLIN. A10 - Monthly pricing is not needed for the base one time installation, that should be FFP. Q11-Would the facility like the option, on the mini split systems, to turn the heat on during the winter months, or would like the systems to be cool only? A11 - Yes, all units installed will be dual use (Cooling and Heating) as they currently are. Q12-Is there a particular brand of choice for the systems? would they like direct replacements or will a different brand work like Daikin Systems? A12: The government is relying on proposals to recommend the best solution to meet the requirements as outlined in the solicitation, statement of work and Q&A. Q13-Would the facility be ok with swapping the voltage of the systems from 110v to 208/230v in the case of the 110v/2Ton systems are not in stock. These units are particularly hard to find in a 2 ton system. A13 - The government is relying on proposals to recommend the best solution to meet the requirements as outlined in the solicitation, statement of work and Q&A. Q14-Can we get verification of the correct tonnage of each of the units? There were some discrepancy`s during the site visit. A14 - The following is the final equipment configuration by location. It supersedes the equipment descriptions in the original Statement of Work, the CLIN 0001 description, and the combined synopsis, and is incorporated by this amendment. Turtle Hospital: Three (3) ductless mini-split systems. Two (2) at 2.5-ton nominal capacity and one (1) at 2-ton nominal capacity. Wet Lab Observers Area: One (1) 3-ton split system tying into the existing ductwork. This system is not ductless. The existing ductwork will be reused. The existing coil is presumed unserviceable and shall be replaced with an indoor unit matched to the new condensing unit. Turtle Barn Aquaculture Area: One (1) new ductless mini-split at 2-ton nominal capacity with two (2) 1-ton indoor heads, one head serving each room. All five (5) systems shall be heat pumps providing both heating and cooling. All equipment shall meet the coastal corrosion protection and materials requirements of the Statement of Work as modified by A39. Where the original Statement of Work, CLIN 0001, or the combined synopsis conflicts with the above, this answer governs. Q15 - Please confirm required size of each condenser and head unit for the Turtle Hospital building. There was some confusion on what was requested vs what we were told. A15 - Answered in question 1 and 14 above Q16 - Do we need to replace all lines between inside and outside unit? A16 - The government is relying on proposals to recommend the best solution to meet the requirements Q17 - Please confirm a size on outdoor unit at the observation building. It doesn't have a tag. A17 - Based on future use it is recommended a three ton split unit. That will tie into the existing duct work. Q18 - Please confirm that duct and coil will be reused inside of observation building. A18 - The duct yes, the coil is presumed to be unserviceable. The Split unit should have an internal unit that will tie into the duct work. Q19 - New unit for Turtle Barn - does the supply power need to be included, or will it be provided by others during office construction? A19- NOAA will provide connection Q20 - Could you provide site-visit photos, equipment photos, measurements, or field notes available for review? A20 - The government does not have existing photos available for review. Vendors were advised to attend the one scheduled site visit to acquire necessary photos etc. Q21 - For the four replacement systems, should the existing refrigerant line sets be reused or replaced? If replacement is required, can approximate lengths and routes be provided? A21 - The government is relying on proposals to recommend the best solution to meet the requirements Q22 - Please confirm the existing electrical service for each system, including voltage, phase, breaker size, disconnect location, and whether the existing circuits may be reused. A22 - Existing circuits and disconnects will be reused. Vendors were advised to attend the one scheduled site visit to acquire necessary photos etc, opportunities were given throughout the site visit. Q23 - For the new 3-ton dual-head system in the Turtle Barn/Aquaculture Area, are the locations of the outdoor condenser and two indoor heads predetermined? A23 - The general locations are established. The outdoor condensing unit will be located on the exterior of the Turtle Barn, and one indoor head will serve each of the two rooms in the Aquaculture Area, each approximately 150 square feet. title: Defense Innovation Unit (DIU) Commercial Solutions Opening (CSO)
description: The Defense Innovation Unit (DIU) is interested in awarding funding agreements (Agreements) to nontraditional and traditional defense contractors to carry out prototype projects that are directly relevant to enhancing the mission effectiveness of military personnel and the supporting platforms, systems, components, or materials proposed to be acquired or developed by the Department of Defense (DoD), or to improvement of platforms, systems, components, or materials in use by the Armed Forces of the United States. As such, DIU hereby announces the release of their streamlined Commercial Solutions Opening (CSO). This CSO is seeking proposals for innovative, commercial technologies that accelerate attainment of asymmetric defense capabilities. In this context, innovative means any new technology, process, or business practice, or any new application of an existing technology, process, or business practice that contributes to the sustainment of global peace and U.S. national security. Agreements will be sought under an open (available for five (5) years), competitive (solution brief/demonstration followed by proposal) CSO. This CSO is considered a competitive process, intended to ensure that competitive procedures are used to the maximum extent practicable when entering into Agreements to carry out these prototype projects. Interested parties with current or new/developmental innovative technological solutions or enhancements are highly encouraged to visit the DIU website to obtain more information regarding the process of presenting their solutions to DIU and the potential for securing said Agreements under this CSO. Topic Areas of Interest (AoI) will be posted on the DIU website and may be updated at any time. Please note that the submission period for solution briefs under the identified AOI's will be open for a limited period of time, so check the DIU website for updates frequently. DIU's website is: https://www.diu.mil/work-with-us

title: PIMC - Fire Alarm Replacement Services
description: The Indian Health Service (IHS), Phoenix Area Office, intends to award a Firm-Fixed-Price contract for the PIMC Fire Alarm Replacement Project (Project PH26PH02H7) at the Phoenix Indian Medical Center (PIMC), 4212 N. 16th Street, Phoenix, Arizona 85016. The Contractor shall provide all labor, materials, equipment, supervision, programming, testing, commissioning, training, and other resources necessary to remove and replace the existing fire alarm control panel (FACP) and graphical user interface (GUI) system. The requirement includes replacement of the existing NOTIFIER NFS-640 Fire Alarm Control Panel with a NOTIFIER INSPIRE N16x Fire Alarm Control Panel, or approved equal, and replacement of the existing GUI/workstation system with the latest NOTIFIER ONYXWorks GUI workstation system, or approved equal. The replacement system shall be fully compatible with the existing NOTIFIER fire alarm system, field devices, loops, and associated components that will remain in place. The Contractor shall be a current NOTIFIER Engineered Systems Distributor (ESD) or authorized NOTIFIER distributor, as specified in the Statement of Work, and shall demonstrate experience installing, programming, commissioning, and servicing networked NOTIFIER systems of comparable size and complexity, including ONYXWorks graphical workstations and healthcare occupancies. The work includes, but is not limited to, fire alarm control panel replacement; annunciator replacement; ONYXWorks GUI installation and configuration; required NOTIFIER network hardware; development and implementation of an updated points list; floor plan and device mapping; programming; system integration; testing and commissioning in accordance with NFPA 72; system cutover and phasing; and on-site training for Government personnel. Place of Performance: Phoenix Indian Medical Center 4212 N. 16th Street Phoenix, AZ 85016 Period of Performance: 100 calendar days from the date of the Notice to Proceed (NTP). Quoters shall review the solicitation, Statement of Work, and all attachments for the complete requirements, submission instructions, and evaluation criteria. All questions and quotations shall be submitted in accordance with the instructions contained in the solicitation.

title: FY27-28 Pediatric Flu Vaccines
description: The Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) awards contracts to the manufacturers of pediatric vaccines for the purchase of standard commercial pediatric vaccines. Vaccines are one of the most cost-effective ways to prevent disease and reduce healthcare costs. The Vaccine for Children (VFC) program, established pursuant to Section 13631 of the Omnibus Budget Reconciliation Act of 1993 (OBRA �93), guarantees federal support for the purchase and supply of sufficient quantities of vaccine to the States to cover a defined group of children. The program helps assure the implementation of effective immunization practices and proper use of vaccines to achieve higher immunization coverage. Children (18 years-of-age or younger) who qualify for immunization through the VFC purchase program include those who are (1) Medicaid-eligible, (2) without health insurance, (3) American Indian/Alaska native (as defined in Subsection (h)(3) of the OBRA �93), or (4) children with health insurance, which does not cover the cost of vaccines, if they receive their immunizations at a Federally-qualified health center or rural health clinic (as defined by the Social Security Act). Health care providers who agree to certain requirements are eligible through the States to receive free vaccine through this VFC purchase program. The establishment of these contracts provides an opportunity to utilize VFC funds and Section 317 vaccine purchase funds to obtain vaccines at prices below those available in the commercial marketplace. In addition, awardees may opt to purchase additional quantities of vaccine under any resulting contract to provide immunizations for children who are not federally vaccine-eligible children using state and local funds. Offerors for this requirement must be manufacturers of pediatric vaccines in accordance with 42 U.S.C. � 1396s. The term "manufacturer" means any corporation, organization, or institution, whether public or private (including Federal, State, and local departments, agencies, and instrumentalities), which manufactures, imports, processes, or distributes under its label any pediatric vaccine. The term "manufacture" means to manufacture, import, process, or distribute a vaccine.

title: AdvM Call for Solutions - Automated Parts Handling for Plating in SOD
description: The Army Contracting Command � Redstone Arsenal (ACC-RSA), on behalf of Tobyhanna Army Depot (TYAD), is seeking innovative solutions to automate and modernize its Plating Shop operations. The Government requires a comprehensive, fully functioning solution consisting of a suite of hardware, automated parts handling equipment, and open-architecture Supervisory Control and Data Acquisition (SCADA) software to perform all aspects of chemical electroplating, conversion coating, and automated shop operations across its 12 different lines/processes. Implementing automation within this operation is vital for modernizing TYAD's capabilities. Proactively deploying this technology will provide significant benefits, including the reduction of employee exposure to hazardous chemicals, increased quality of final products, increased throughput, decreased operational costs, digital recipe management, and the addition of safety and alarming systems to alert personnel in the event of a system malfunction. The full Call for Solutions document (.pdf), detailing the problem statement, desired solution objectives, submission requirements, and evaluation phases, is available in the "Attachments" section below. All Solution Briefs and questions regarding this Call must be submitted via email to Contracting Officer Stephanie Dillon and Contract Specialist Benjamin Hymas at usarmy.redstone.acc.mbx.acc-rsa-advm-cso@army.mil. The deadline to submit Solution Briefs for Phase 1 is Wednesday, 16 September 2026 at 12:00 PM Central Daylight Time (CST). title: Electrosurgical unit (ESU)
description: All equipment shall be newly manufactured. It shall not be used, refurbished, reconditioned, remanufactured, or previously used for demonstration. Salient characteristics and any single-source need The salient physical, functional, and performance characteristics the equipment must meet are stated under Minimum technical requirements below: Minimum technical requirements The equipment shall meet the following minimum requirements. Display and user interface A touchscreen display for user interaction and parameter control Tissue impedance monitoring Monitoring of tissue impedance at a minimum rate of 434,000 times per second, providing real-time feedback and energy delivery adjustment Output frequency Output frequency within the range of 400 kHz to 500 kHz Operating modes The equipment shall support the following operating modes. Monopolar CUT (Pure) Monopolar CUT (Blend) Monopolar COAG (Fulgurate) Monopolar COAG (Spray) Monopolar COAG (Soft) Bipolar coagulation Vessel sealing Electrical and safety Compliance with all applicable Federal, state, and local safety standards Required accessories The contractor shall provide all accessories necessary to fully operate the equipment in every operating mode listed above. At minimum the following shall be included. Monopolar electrode and holster with switch, compatible with all monopolar modes. Patient return electrode for monopolar operation. Bipolar forceps, cord, and footswitch for bipolar coagulation. Vessel sealer with switch for vessel sealing mode. All accessories shall be compatible with the delivered equipment and ready for use upon delivery.

title: FY27-28 Pediatric Flu Vaccines
description: The Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) awards contracts to the manufacturers of pediatric vaccines for the purchase of standard commercial pediatric vaccines. Vaccines are one of the most cost-effective ways to prevent disease and reduce healthcare costs. The Vaccine for Children (VFC) program, established pursuant to Section 13631 of the Omnibus Budget Reconciliation Act of 1993 (OBRA �93), guarantees federal support for the purchase and supply of sufficient quantities of vaccine to the States to cover a defined group of children. The program helps assure the implementation of effective immunization practices and proper use of vaccines to achieve higher immunization coverage. Children (18 years-of-age or younger) who qualify for immunization through the VFC purchase program include those who are (1) Medicaid-eligible, (2) without health insurance, (3) American Indian/Alaska native (as defined in Subsection (h)(3) of the OBRA �93), or (4) children with health insurance, which does not cover the cost of vaccines, if they receive their immunizations at a Federally-qualified health center or rural health clinic (as defined by the Social Security Act). Health care providers who agree to certain requirements are eligible through the States to receive free vaccine through this VFC purchase program. The establishment of these contracts provides an opportunity to utilize VFC funds and Section 317 vaccine purchase funds to obtain vaccines at prices below those available in the commercial marketplace. In addition, awardees may opt to purchase additional quantities of vaccine under any resulting contract to provide immunizations for children who are not federally vaccine-eligible children using state and local funds. Offerors for this requirement must be manufacturers of pediatric vaccines in accordance with 42 U.S.C. � 1396s. The term "manufacturer" means any corporation, organization, or institution, whether public or private (including Federal, State, and local departments, agencies, and instrumentalities), which manufactures, imports, processes, or distributes under its label any pediatric vaccine. The term "manufacture" means to manufacture, import, process, or distribute a vaccine.

title: FY27-28 Adult Flu Vaccines
description: The Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) awards one or more Indefinite Delivery/Indefinite Quantity (ID/IQ) contracts for the purchase of standard commercial adult vaccines. The establishment of these contracts provides opportunity to utilize Section 317 vaccine purchase funds to obtain vaccines at prices below those available in the commercial marketplace. These funds provide vaccines for state and local health departments to use in populations at greatest risk for under vaccination and disease. The 317 program as established under Section 317(j) of the Public Health Service Act, works to ensure that adults receive appropriate immunization by partnering with healthcare providers in the public and private sectors. The program helps assure the implementation of effective immunization practices and proper use of vaccines to achieve higher immunization coverage. The vaccines awarded under these contracts will be purchased for the National Center for Immunization and Respiratory Disease�s (NCIRD�s) immunization awardees (the fifty state health departments, several large city programs, and current and former U.S. Territories) to support adult immunization programs as provided under Section 317(j) of the Public Health Service Act. In addition, awardees may opt to purchase additional quantities of vaccine for adults under any resulting contract using state and local funds.

description: The purpose of this acquisition is to have Health Effects Laboratory Division (HELD) centrifuges undergo preventative maintenance and calibration. Regular calibration of centrifuges is essential because it ensures that rotational speed, temperature control (when applicable), and timing functions remain accurate, which directly affects the reliability and reproducibility of experimental results. The vendor shall perform visual and functional checks for rotor condition, imbalance indicators, lid locks, refrigeration performance (where applicable), and overall mechanical integrity. Key parameters will be calibrated according to International Standard Organization (ISO) 17025 standards.

title: 15 Foot offset flex arm for Bat Wing mowers
description: The 15-foot offset flex arm rotary cutter requires heavy-duty 11L by 15, 12-ply tires with a minimum load capacity of 4,000 pounds. It must be capable of cutting directly in-line with the tractor or at any offset distance up to 122 inches (10.16 feet). The assembly requires a minimum two-and-a-half-inch castor pivot shaft, six-bolt hubs with at least a 6,000-pound capacity, and bolt-in replaceable axles. Major pivot points must utilize spring steel tension bushings and induction-hardened pins. Hydraulic and mechanical requirements include a minimum of four hydraulic circuits with independent wing lift for the 15-foot mower, a heavy-duty three-and-a-half by 36-inch welded hydraulic cylinder, and an optional six-port selector valve kit for independent wing action on tractors with limited hydraulic outlets. Power delivery requires a minimum rating of 200 horsepower at 1,000 RPM while accommodating 540 RPM power delivery from the tractor. A safety lighting kit is also required. Standard travel dimensions must maintain a maximum width of 70 inches to the left of the tractor and 52 inches to the right, totaling 121 inches for the arm and rotary cutter assembly. When operating with the stop block installed on the transport lock bar designed to improve clearance for oncoming traffic on narrow roads the dimensions are configured to 55 inches to the left of the tractor and 66 inches to the right (totaling 121 inches).

title: 15 Foot offset flex arm for Bat Wing mowers
description: The 15-foot offset flex arm rotary cutter requires heavy-duty 11L by 15, 12-ply tires with a minimum load capacity of 4,000 pounds. It must be capable of cutting directly in-line with the tractor or at any offset distance up to 122 inches (10.16 feet). The assembly requires a minimum two-and-a-half-inch castor pivot shaft, six-bolt hubs with at least a 6,000-pound capacity, and bolt-in replaceable axles. Major pivot points must utilize spring steel tension bushings and induction-hardened pins. Hydraulic and mechanical requirements include a minimum of four hydraulic circuits with independent wing lift for the 15-foot mower, a heavy-duty three-and-a-half by 36-inch welded hydraulic cylinder, and an optional six-port selector valve kit for independent wing action on tractors with limited hydraulic outlets. Power delivery requires a minimum rating of 200 horsepower at 1,000 RPM while accommodating 540 RPM power delivery from the tractor. A safety lighting kit is also required. Standard travel dimensions must maintain a maximum width of 70 inches to the left of the tractor and 52 inches to the right, totaling 121 inches for the arm and rotary cutter assembly. When operating with the stop block installed on the transport lock bar designed to improve clearance for oncoming traffic on narrow roads the dimensions are configured to 55 inches to the left of the tractor and 66 inches to the right (totaling 121 inches).

title: USFS R6 Slide in Water Tank
description: This is a combined synopsis/solicitation for commercial items prepared in accordance with the format in Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) Subpart 12.6, as supplemented with additional information included in this notice. Quotations are being requested. The U.S. Forest Service (Gifford Pinchot National Forest, Wind River Ranger District) requires the acquisition of a brand-new, commercial-grade, slide-in water tank unit. This system will be deployed in an existing government-owned dump truck host vehicle and operated primarily on rough, unpaved, and mountainous U.S. Forest Service access roads. EXCLUSIONS: This acquisition explicitly DOES NOT include the purchase or provision of a new dump truck vehicle body. INCLUSIONS: This requirement is strictly for the fabrication, testing, and turn-key delivery of the complete slide-in water tank unit and matching securement hardware kit as detailed below 2. Schedule of Items (CLIN Structure) This procurement is conducted under FAR Part 12 Simplified Acquisition Procedures [12.203]. Bidders must submit a Firm-Fixed-Price (FFP) quote covering all items to be considered responsive: CLIN 0001: Slide-in Water Tank Unit (2,600 - 3,000 Gallon Capacity, as specified) | Qty: 1 | Unit: EA CLIN 0002: Shipping and Handling: FOB Destination to Carson, WA 98610. (Note: Shipping costs will be evaluated but only executed if the successful contractor's facility is located outside the 100-mile local government pickup radius). 3. Core Technical Salient Characteristics Summary The manufactured water tank system must conform strictly to the mechanical and physical boundaries of the government's host vehicle (2013 Freightliner M2, 4-Axle Dump Truck equipped with a drop axle). Physical Footprint Box Constraints: Main Tank Truck Box Clearance: Main tank structure must drop cleanly into the truck bed box dimensions (180�L � 72�W � 54�H). Ultimate System Maximum Footprint: Total overall footprint of the completed assembly�inclusive of the tank box shell, rear plumbing manifolds, auxiliary pumps, engines, utility reels, and guards�must not exceed 216� Long � 72� Wide � 66� High. Rear Overhang Allowance: Bidders are permitted to utilize up to a 216-inch overall footprint length, allowing the rear subframe, auxiliary pump assembly, plumbing manifold, and brush guard to overhang past the 180-inch rear edge of the dump bed floor. Capacity & Fluid Control: Minimum 2,600-gallon operational fluid capacity required, with a target performance goal of 3,000 gallons. Built with engineered internal lateral and longitudinal baffles to control intense liquid surge on off-road terrain. Structural Integration & Support Legs: Heavy-duty tie-down loops or D-rings welded onto the front and rear faces of a 5-inch steel tube perimeter subframe. Must feature an integrated, self-contained structural storage stand or folding drop-leg support jacks capable of supporting the fully evacuated weight of the unit to allow for independent loading and unloading without requiring external heavy machinery (cranes or forklifts). Standalone Pump & Engine Setup: High-performance, single-stage centrifugal transfer/fire pump matching or exceeding 110 GPM at 100 PSI (High-Pressure) and 430 GPM at 25 PSI (High-Volume). Equipped with an integrated priming system capable of self-loading/draft from a static environmental water source. Completely self-powered via a dedicated auxiliary engine (minimum 23 HP, V-Twin gas or diesel equivalent) with an independent 5-gallon fuel tank. Vehicle PTO, hydrostatic, or hydraulic-driven pump systems are strictly prohibited. Auxiliary Equipment Protection: If any part of the motor, pump assembly, or hose reel hangs past the truck bed floor, an integrated steel tubular wrap-around brush guard/cage is mandatory to shield mechanical parts from backing impacts and flying debris. Plumbing System: Minimum 2.5-inch hydrant fill pipeline with female NST swivel connector and anti-backflow mechanism; pneumatic multi-nozzle rear spray system linked directly to the truck's service/brake air supply lines; dedicated 2.5-inch and 1.5-inch discharge systems with quarter-turn manual ball valves; a 4-inch rapid gravity evacuation butterfly dump valve; and an integrated 1.5-inch � 50-foot heavy-duty pre-plumbed utility hose reel. 4. Evaluation Criteria & Basis for Award Quotes will be evaluated under FAR 12.203. Award will be made to the responsible offeror whose quotation represents the most advantageous solution to the Government, considering the following three evaluation factors: Technical Acceptability: The degree to which the offered tank assembly meets or exceeds the mandatory technical salient characteristics. Delivery Timeline: The contractor�s verified capability to manufacture, test, and deliver the completed unit within the mandatory 60-calendar-day performance period. Price: Evaluated to ensure the final proposed price is fair and reasonable. 5. Submission Instructions for Offerors Quotation Package Structure: To be considered responsive, packages must be organized in the following order: SF-1449 Form: Completed and signed in Blocks 17a, 30a, 30b, and 30c (Legibly list Company Name, Telephone, Email, and SAM Unique Entity ID (UEI) in Block 17a). SF-30 Amendments: Signed copies acknowledging all formal amendments issued (if applicable). Schedule of Items Pricing: Complete the firm-fixed pricing grid for CLIN 0001 and CLIN 0002. Technical Evaluation & Delivery Documents: Submit a fully filled out and signed copy of Attachment 1 (Requirements Compliance Checklist) detailing any equivalents A basic Product Layout Sketch or Drawing proving the completed assembly satisfies the 216�L � 72�W � 66�H boundary envelopment parameters A brief Delivery Milestone Schedule confirming production capacity to hit the 60-day deadline. description: The Government (138th FW) intends to enter into a Firm Fixed Price Blanket Purchase Agreement (BPA) that will consist of a three (3) year ordering period of October 31, 2026 to October 30, 2029, with 3-5 different small businesses. This combined synopsis/solicitation is being used to set up agreements that will be used to place orders for lodging. The resulting Blanket Purchase Agreements (BPA) are not a contract but an agreement of pricing, terms, and conditions to allow for quick and efficient execution of delivery orders for lodging to benefit Air National Guard members in a Unit Training Assembly (UTA) status. The physical address of any property for any requirement for lodging in Tulsa, OK must be within 20 driving miles of 9100 E 46th St N, Tulsa, OK, 74115. Due to AT/OPSEC requirements, only limited dates for known required lodging will be provided in this Performance Work Statement for predetermined UTA training periods; additional dates shall be provided at the time of any resultant award to an interested party who provides a successful offer. This combined synopsis/solicitation is 100% set aside for small business in accordance with RFO 19.104-1. No 3rd party vendors will be considered. All firms responding must be registered with the System for Award Management (SAM). All responsive quotes will be considered by the agency. All questions concerning this combined synopsis/solicitation must be directed to 138.FW.MSC@us.af.mil by 10:00am Central time zone on 9 September 2026. You may email your quote to 138.FW.MSC@us.af.mil no later than 16 September 2026 at 1:00PM Central Daylight Time. It is incumbent upon the interested parties to verify that your quote has been received by our office. Invoicing will be required to go through Wide Area Work Flow (WAWF) module of the PIEE website (https://piee.eb.mil).
